redraw.requested: Owner approved redrawing the whole Potez in the crew pixel-art style, with static body and separate animated crew, propeller and rear gun.

assets.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit / style-transfer. Production game sprite redraw of the EXACT Potez 25 biplane in reference image 1, in a coherent restrained PIXEL-ART style matching the tiny leather-helmeted aircrew of reference image 2 (style reference ONLY). Keep the aircraft's exact RIGHT-FACING STRICT SIDE PROFILE, silhouette, proportions, tandem open cockpit locations, upper wing and strut locations, fixed landing gear, tail, engine and nose shape. Original intended canvas 400 x 173; the aircraft must retain that aspect ratio and placement after downsampling. This is the same recognized aircraft, not a new model. Keep muted olive/forest green paint, readable dark pixel outlines and spare 2-3 tone grouped shading, subtle olive highlights, sparse mechanical details at the final game display width of 220 px. Existing plane is too flat compared to crew: add coherent pixel clusters, not realistic painterly texture. Preserve the PARTISAN markings from image 1: white numeral 8 on fuselage, circular white roundel with red five-point star on rear fuselage, vertical blue-white-red rudder band with red star, in their same positions. IMPORTANT MODULAR PARTS: render ONLY THE EMPTY AIRFRAME. Remove BOTH crew figures if any; its two cockpits stay OPEN and transparent, as reference image 1. Remove the existing small rear gun above the aft cockpit; keep only the low fixed cockpit rim. Remove the entire nose propeller blades and spinner: the propeller is a SEPARATE animated asset, so terminate the nose at the mounting point without any painted stationary propeller. No people, no weapons, no propeller blades, no motion blur, no shadow, no smoke, no sky, no ground, no extra insignia or text labels. Genuine transparent background, all holes between struts and open cockpits remain transparent. One complete aircraft only, all extremities inside the canvas. Prefer crisp 1-pixel final edges and simple readable shapes, no chunky toy proportions and no thick white contour.

Precise historical video-game livery edit. Image 1 is the finished EMPTY pixel-art Potez 25 airframe master, 400 x 173, side view facing RIGHT. Image 2 is the existing accepted historical alternative livery. Change ONLY the two insignia regions of image 1 to match image 2: (1) replace the tail's blue/white/red vertical band and red star with the same olive-green tail paint and small red-white checker shield located on the tail as in image 2; (2) replace the round white fuselage roundel/red star with the red-white checker shield as in image 2. Retain the white number 8 exactly where it is. Do NOT add any other emblems, letters, flags, insignia or text. This is neutral historical artwork for a game, not advocacy. Preserve absolutely all geometry, silhouette, scale, alignment, empty open cockpit holes, olive pixel shading, highlights, dark edges, wing, struts, landing gear, engine and nose of image 1. No people, no guns, no nose propeller blades, no background, no shadow. Genuine transparent PNG. One full plane only in the same 400 x 173 frame and same right-facing strict side profile.

Production modular pixel-art asset for the RIGHT-FACING SIDE-VIEW Potez 25 biplane in the reference. Draw ONLY its detached two-bladed nose propeller at REST, seen strictly FROM THE SIDE, with its shaft axis horizontal, two blades extending vertically UP and DOWN from a small central hub. The whole sprite must be very NARROW and TALL, approximately 1:7 width-to-height, not a frontal fan. Small compact olive-gray metal central spinner/hub, thin gray steel blades with a little restrained warm-gray shading and subtly different lit/shaded blade faces. Plain early-aircraft two-blade design preserving the reference's simple silhouette. Sparse crisp readable pixel clusters and thin dark edges, matching an olive 2D pixel-art WWII biplane displayed at 220 px wide. Final intended propeller cell is 20 x 128 pixels; no microscopic texture. Full blades and hub must be entirely visible, centered vertically and horizontally, with equal transparent margin above and below. Genuine transparent background. No aircraft, people, weapons, additional props, base, shadows, motion blur, text, numbers, labels or guide lines. A SINGLE narrow vertical side-view propeller, not multiple variants.

Production subtle idle sprite animation of the EXACT two adult leather-helmeted aircrew busts from reference 1, for the tiny open cockpits of reference 2. Output a strict FOUR columns by TWO rows grid: eight equal square cells, one single complete helmet-to-waist bust per cell, all same scale and fixed waist baseline. TOP ROW, four frames: the PILOT faces RIGHT, same person as the right-hand figure of reference 1, arms held low forward to unseen controls. BOTTOM ROW, four frames: the OBSERVER faces LEFT, same person as the left-hand figure of reference 1, arms low forward as if resting at a separately drawn rear gun; NO gun painted into the figure. Across each four-frame loop change ONLY a tiny breathing lift in chest/shoulder and a minimal natural head adjustment/blink; hand grip positions and waist stay fixed, no whole-body translation, no arm swings, no dramatic head turns. Frames 1 and 4 meet smoothly. Each person must retain the exact same helmet, goggles, face, clothing, outline, earthy brown/tan/olive colors, mature realistic proportions and sparse pixel-cluster style in all four frames. These figures will be about 23 x 26 source pixels and just 13 px high on screen: keep each change small and readable, not detailed painting or cute/cartoon faces. All eight busts completely fit inside their own equal cells, generous transparent gutters, no duplicated or crossed cell boundaries. Genuine transparent background. No aircraft, seats, guns, scenery, shadows, symbols, labels, text, numbers or grid lines.

assets.note: The generated left cell faces left and is used as the observer; the right cell faces right and is used as the pilot. The manifest records the actual cell mapping.
assets.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit / identity-preserve. Production raster game asset, WWII Potez 25 biplane crew. Image 1 is the exact plane, side profile facing RIGHT; image 2 is an enlarged crop showing the flat muted green/gray outlined pixel-cluster style and its two tiny OPEN tandem cockpits. Create ONLY the two adult human aircrew upper bodies as separate clean cutouts on one transparent sheet, exactly TWO EQUAL SQUARE CELLS in ONE horizontal row, with generous empty space between them. LEFT CELL: seated PILOT in strict side profile FACING RIGHT (towards the nose), brown leather flying helmet, simple goggles, olive-brown leather flight jacket, both forearms held low forward towards unseen controls. RIGHT CELL: seated REAR OBSERVER/GUNNER in strict side profile FACING LEFT (towards tail), matching brown flight helmet/goggles, muted tan/olive flight jacket, both forearms held low forward to the left as if holding a separate ring-mounted gun. NO weapons painted into these figures: the gun must be a separate rotating asset. Both figures are busts from helmet to waist, seated posture (leaning only slightly forward), adult realistic proportions, serious neutral faces, no oversized heads, no cute/cartoon look. One pilot and one observer, exactly two people total. No chairs, seats, cockpit parts, fuselage, airplane, props, floor, terrain, shadows, insignia, flags, badges, text or cell borders. Style MUST match the source: sparse crisp pixel clusters, tiny dark outline, restrained flat shading, earthy brown/tan/gray-green palette. These will be displayed as about 14 x 24 source-pixel busts, and only 8 x 13 pixels on screen: design very simple readable profiles and helmet/nose silhouettes for that small scale, no high-resolution painted textures, no fine details. Both busts share exactly the same scale, vertical placement and waist baseline, truly transparent backgrounds.

Neutral historical video-game artwork. Recreate the existing aircraft machine-gun visible in this tiny low-resolution reference as a separate 2D pixel-art inventory sprite, viewed from its SIDE and pointing LEFT. It is a flat nonfunctional game drawing, not a real object or technical schematic. Only simple gray metal silhouette and sparse shading, matching the reference palette and pixel-cluster style, for eventual display at 48 by 20 pixels. Short receiver on the right, thin horizontal barrel to the left, small rounded magazine above the receiver. Transparent background and generous padding. Exclude the fixed triangular mounting stand below it; that belongs to the aircraft. No person, airplane, hands, environment, flash, smoke, text, annotations or dimensions.
